intuition.title: Precursor aggregation persists through treatment
intuition.text: The authors contrast loose initial sols with more strongly aggregated ammonia-precipitated suspensions. Microwave-treated suspension particles remain polydisperse; treated sols have narrower distributions and primarily hexagonal outlines. This is a morphological comparison, not a hexagonal-phase assignment.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied main pp.1–3; Figures1–2 and table

intuition.title: Do not merge XRD and microscopy sizes
intuition.text: The table reports coherent-scattering domains separately from TEM averages. Initial rows report XRD <5nm and TEM mean4nm; their prose TEM ranges and optical sol size estimate remain different measurement contexts.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied main pp.1–3; equation1 and table

intuition.title: Additional conditions are not a complete matrix
intuition.text: Some experiments extend microwave treatment to6h without a sample-resolved temperature mapping; suspension CSD stays unchanged. The ordinary hydrothermal comparator reports a typical15nm CSD but no complete temperature/time recipe. No additional crossed variants or digitized distribution points are invented.

intuition.title: Sintering suitability is a proposal
intuition.text: The authors suggest that narrow distributions and weak interparticle contacts may help low-temperature sintering by limiting irreversible pores and favoring uniform ceramics. No sintering experiment or performance measurement is supplied.

intuition.title: Sol stability mechanism is proposed
intuition.text: Authors suggest adsorbed hydroxyl ions can stabilize the sol. Prolonged storage lowers pH to5–6 and accompanies coagulation; no storage duration or direct surface-coverage measurement is given.

general_background.title: Microwave coupling and heating
general_background.summary: Microwave fields couple to materials through their electrical response and can heat different parts of a reaction mixture differently. Polarization and mobile charges dissipate field energy, so heating depends on the liquid, dissolved species and other absorbing materials.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
